title: Lifespan Development
description: Introduces diverse perspectives of child and youth wellbeing and growth as a basis for praxis with children, youth and families. Critically examines development as well as the concepts of child/childhood, youth and adolescence and adult/adulthood. Interrogates the settler colonial, racist, ableist and cisheteronormative practices shaping ideas of development. Promotes critical thinking about health equity and the relevancy of different perspectives to the health and wellbeing of diverse child populations.
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of CYC 120, CYC166A.
Students in the Bachelor of Child and Youth Care program must earn a minimum grade of C+ in all pre- or co-requisites.
